title: Prefill/decode scheduler: phase-splitting policy, fairness knobs, and latency-vs-throughput trade-offs
creator: Rae Patel
description: Design and implement a prefill/decode scheduling policy that explicitly splits request handling into phases, with configurable fairness and latency vs throughput knobs. The goal is to reduce tail latency for interactive short requests, preserve throughput for long batched prefill workloads, and provide guardrails for enterprise SLAs. Work includes scheduler algorithm, feature flags, integration with kernel selection and attention optimization telemetry, and a rollout plan with observability and safety fallbacks.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler supports explicit phase splitting: prefill and decode stages with independent admission/control
Configurable knobs for phase preemption, per-queue tokens, and proportional fairness across request classes
A/B benchmark showing <=10% increase in median latency for long background workloads while 30-50% reduction in 95th/99th tail for interactive short requests compared to baseline
Unit and integration tests covering preemption, priority escalation, and fallback to single-phase handling
Console dashboard (new tiles) showing phase-level queue length, per-request phase latency, fairness metrics, and per-customer SLA compliance
Feature-flagged rollout with automatic revert on >5% error-rate regression or CPU/GPU saturation anomalies
decisions: Adopt a two-tier phase split: PREFILL (KV/cache warmup + attention-heavy computation) and DECODE (autoregressive token generation)
Use proportional fairness with weighted fairness tokens per customer-class instead of strict strict-priority queuing to avoid starvation
Introduce a 'latency_sensitivity' attribute per route (interactive | batch | background) that maps to default scheduling weights
Default phase preemption allowed for interactive routes up to a configurable token budget; background routes can be promoted during low load
Fallback policy: when GPU utilization > threshold, coalesce to single-phase mode for compatibility with older kernels
technical_notes: Interactions with kernel selection: prefill tends to use attention kernels optimized for long sequences (memory-intense), while decode prefers low-latency token kernels. Scheduler must expose phase hints to the kernel selector to prefer low-latency kernels during DECODE. Attention optimizations (rotary/ALiBi placements and fused attention kernels) should be prioritized for PREFILL when sequence_length > 1024. Batching windows: PREFILL batching window = 15ms default, DECODE batching window = 6ms default, both configurable. Implementation will add phase-aware backpressure tokens, per-GPU slot accounting, and a small fast-path for single-token interactive requests that bypass prefill when cache hit is likely.
